# Armybox

> A memory-safe `#[no_std]` BusyBox/Toybox clone written in Rust.

Armybox is a multi-call binary providing 293 Unix utilities in a single, incredibly small executable. Built entirely with `#[no_std]` Rust, it delivers 100% Toybox compatibility plus 55 additional applets in just 108 KB (54 KB with UPX compression). Armybox is ideal for embedded systems, minimal containers (FROM scratch), rescue environments, space-constrained systems, and Android devices.

## Links

- [Documentation](https://pegasusheavy.github.io/armybox/)
- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/pegasusheavy/armybox)
- [Crates.io Package](https://crates.io/crates/armybox)
- [API Docs (docs.rs)](https://docs.rs/armybox)

## Key Features

- 293 applets -- 100% Toybox compatible plus 55 additional utilities
- Multi-call binary -- single executable providing all utilities
- Pure Rust 2024 -- memory-safe implementation using the latest Rust edition
- Incredibly tiny -- 108 KB stripped, ~54 KB with UPX compression (~380 bytes per applet)
- True `#[no_std]` -- no standard library dependency, only `libc` and `alloc`
- Android-native -- first-class Android/Bionic support, works on Android 5.0+
- Embedded-ready -- works on systems without full std support
- Cross-platform -- builds for Linux (glibc/musl), Android, x86_64, ARM64, ARM32
- POSIX.1-2017 compliant -- core utilities follow the POSIX standard
- Includes POSIX shell (sh/ash/dash), vi editor, terminal multiplexer (screen/tmux), and init system
- Full networking suite -- wget, httpd, ip, netcat, ping, traceroute, and more
- Archive and compression -- tar, gzip, bzip2, xz, zip support
- Docker-friendly -- perfect for FROM scratch container images

## Installation

```bash
# Clone and build
git clone https://github.com/pegasusheavy/armybox
cd armybox
cargo build --release

# Install symlinks
sudo ./target/release/armybox --install /usr/local/bin

# Compress with UPX (optional)
upx --best target/release/armybox
```

## Quick Start

```bash
# Direct invocation
./armybox ls -la
./armybox cat file.txt
./armybox sh           # Start POSIX shell
./armybox vi file.txt  # Edit with vi

# List all available applets
./armybox --list

# After installing symlinks, use utilities directly
ls -la
cat file.txt
```
